record.paper_title: Some Open Problems on Multiple Ergodic Averages
record.original_question: Let C_{T,S} be the set of sequences of the form a(n) = ∫ f · T^n g · S^n h dμ, where (X, X, μ, T, S) ranges over all measure-preserving systems and f, g, h are bounded measurable functions, and let C_T be the subclass obtained when T and S are powers of a single transformation. Are these two classes equal, i.e. does every sequence arising from two commuting transformations already arise from powers of one transformation?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let a measure-preserving system be a quadruple $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu,T)$ where $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu)$ is a standard probability space and $T:X\to X$ is an invertible measurable map preserving $\mu$. Two such transformations $T,S$ on $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu)$ are said to commute if $T\circ S=S\circ T$.

Define two classes of sequences indexed by $n\in\mathbb{Z}$:

(i) Let $\mathcal{C}_{T,S}$ be the set of all sequences of the form
$$a(n)=\int_X f\cdot (T^n g)\cdot (S^n h)\,d\mu,\qquad n\in\mathbb{Z},$$
where $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu)$ ranges over all standard probability spaces, $T$ and $S$ range over all pairs of commuting measure-preserving transformations of $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu)$, and $f,g,h\in L^\infty(\mu)$.

(ii) Let $\mathcal{C}_T$ be the subclass consisting of those sequences in $\mathcal{C}_{T,S}$ that arise when $T$ and $S$ are integer powers of a single measure-preserving transformation $R$, i.e. $T=R^k$, $S=R^\ell$ for some $k,\ell\in\mathbb{Z}$.

Question: Does the equality $\mathcal{C}_{T,S}=\mathcal{C}_T$ hold? That is, is every correlation sequence arising from a pair of commuting measure-preserving transformations also realizable as a correlation sequence using only powers of a single measure-preserving transformation?
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial partial progress is known: it has been proved that any sequence in C_{T,S} (for commuting T,S) can be decomposed as a nilsequence plus an error term that is small in uniform density, matching what was previously known for the single-transformation class C_T. This yields striking consequences (e.g., convergence results for commuting transformations reducing to the one-transformation case) but does not establish the full equality C_{T,S}=C_T, which appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Multiple correlation sequences and nilsequences
status_evidence.snippet: Any such correlation sequence is the sum of a nilsequence and an error term that is small in uniform density; this was previously known only for measure preserving actions of a single transformation.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress: a structural decomposition (nilsequence + small error) is established for correlation sequences of commuting transformations, but the exact equality C_{T,S}=C_T is not claimed.

status_evidence.title: A decomposition of multicorrelation sequences for commuting transformations along primes
status_evidence.snippet: Decomposition of multicorrelation sequences for commuting transformations.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent works continue to obtain decompositions for commuting transformations, indicating the equality question is approached via structure theorems rather than fully resolved.
